title: Berkshire 1993: Concentration, Real Risk, and Holding Wonderful Businesses
summary: Buffett's 1993 letter argues risk is loss of purchasing power, not beta, and that concentrating in a few understandable, moat-protected businesses beats diversification. It also covers float economics, super-cat discipline, tax-deferred compounding, Dexter Shoe, and governance.

principles.text: Real risk is failing to preserve purchasing power after taxes and inflation, not stock volatility (beta).
principles.quote: the real risk that an investor must assess is whether his aggregate after-tax receipts from an investment (including those he receives on sale) will, over his prospective holding period, give him at least as much purchasing power as he had to begin with, plus a modest rate of interest on that initial stake.

principles.text: If you understand business economics, concentrate on your best few ideas; conventional diversification hurts results and adds risk.
principles.quote: if you are a know-something investor, able to understand business economics and to find five to ten sensibly-priced companies that possess important long-term competitive advantages, conventional diversification makes no sense for you.

principles.text: Volatility is an opportunity: a manic Mr. Market periodically prices solid businesses irrationally low.
principles.quote: The more manic-depressive this chap is, the greater the opportunities available to the investor.

principles.text: Hold a piece of an outstanding business with the tenacity of an owner of the whole business.
principles.quote: An investor should ordinarily hold a small piece of an outstanding business with the same tenacity that an owner would exhibit if he owned all of that business.

principles.text: Brands, products and distribution create a protective moat; commodity-like businesses have no such defense.
principles.quote: The might of their brand names, the attributes of their products, and the strength of their distribution systems give them an enormous competitive advantage, setting up a protective moat around their economic castles.

principles.text: Avoid fast-changing industries you cannot evaluate; stick to easy-to-understand cases.
principles.quote: Why search for a needle buried in a haystack when one is sitting in plain sight?
